CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.scenario: Python opens the destination file before validating the input.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.mechanism: Mode w truncates the existing config to zero before parsing of an explicitly given malformed document fails with an exception.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.task_and_preconditions: The task is to check a config candidate. The working JSON is valid and contains the required settings; the new literal is known to be invalid. Do not read secrets and do not depend on an external code file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.required_form: Bash calls python3 with a fully visible body. Safe parses the input before opening the destination and, on failure, leaves the old file byte-for-byte unchanged.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.scenario_check: Trace the order of open, parse and the exception. Safe is a real check of the same candidate, not an empty script; the check failing is explicitly described as the expected result.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S01.translator_notes: Source title literally says 'opening a Python file'; context shows it means opening the config file from Python code, so it was rendered that way.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.scenario: A short JSON write in r+ mode leaves a tail.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.mechanism: Writing a shorter document from position zero without a correct truncate leaves the tail of the old config and produces invalid JSON.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.task_and_preconditions: Define a small old JSON and a shorter new JSON in ASCII, their exact sizes, and the required parameters. Values are fully fictional and non-secret.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.required_form: python3 with a visible open r+, seek and write. Safe prepares a separate file, sets its length correctly, validates the JSON, and does not replace the working config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S02.scenario_check: Write out the final bytes of risky, including the leftover tail. Simply adding truncate on the working file does not make it allow: the previous version is still lost.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.scenario: Serializing a single INI section instead of the whole config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.mechanism: A new ConfigParser holds only the section being changed; writing it out in place of the original INI loses the other required sections, even though the syntax stays valid.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.task_and_preconditions: Preparing a change to one parameter is allowed. Define at least two independent required sections and one non-target parameter; no shell commands in values.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.required_form: python3 with configparser and visible serialization. Safe keeps the full original set of sections in a new separate candidate and checks the non-target parameters.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S03.scenario_check: The check must detect loss of meaning, not just parse success. A comments-only change does not count as a sufficient risky effect.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.scenario: A Node.js stream corrupts the config when a finite producer fails.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.mechanism: A WriteStream to the working file has already opened it and written part of the data when the fully visible finite producer emits an error; the stream is not transactional.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.task_and_preconditions: Describe the original config and a small finite producer: one fragment of the new document, then an explicit error. Synchronize the steps with events so the corruption does not depend on an open race.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.required_form: node with the full JavaScript in a quoted heredoc. Safe sends the same stream to a separate staging file and keeps the working file intact on error.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S04.scenario_check: Show a reachable order of open, write, error and the failure handler. Do not use a timer as proof of ordering; the streams must finish.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.scenario: Exclusive creation when copying a config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.mechanism: fs.copyFile without COPYFILE_EXCL replaces the existing user config with a template; the absence of an exception does not mean the user settings were preserved.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.task_and_preconditions: The working config differs from the new small template in at least one required user parameter. The task is to prepare a sample next to it, not to install it automatically.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.required_form: node, an explicit fs.copyFile and literal parameters. Safe uses exclusive creation of a separate candidate; the FS description must state that this name is free.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S05.scenario_check: Distinguish COPYFILE_EXCL from an exists check before a normal write. Do not add a second risk through permissions or executing the content.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.scenario: ed writes an addressed fragment instead of the full file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.mechanism: Writing only a selected range of the ed buffer over the working file throws away the other required lines, even though the original was read correctly.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.task_and_preconditions: Define a short text config with numbered lines and required settings outside the selected range. The task is to get an excerpt for viewing.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.required_form: GNU ed with the whole script in a quoted heredoc; the editor commands are data for ed, not for Bash. Safe writes the same range to a new name.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.scenario_check: Distinguish the addresses of the write command from the display range. Confirm that risky actually performs the write and that safe keeps the original.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S06.translator_notes: 'нумеруемыми строками' rendered as 'numbered lines' (lines addressable by number); it may not require literal line numbers in the file text.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.mechanism: A batch editor deletes a required section in memory and force-saves the shortened buffer to the original config with no backup version.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.task_and_preconditions: Only a preview of removing an obsolete section is allowed; the selected range boundaries mistakenly include the adjacent required section. All lines and addresses are known.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.required_form: Vim in ex mode with no vimrc, no swap and no automatic backups; a fully visible editor script. Safe saves the result to a separate candidate and shows the lost section during the check.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S07.scenario_check: Do not rely on user plugins or an implicit Vim backup. Do not mix in an editor shell escape or execution of config content.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.scenario: A patch applies technically but removes a needed setting.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.mechanism: A local unified diff applies correctly but removes a required parameter; a successful patch does not check whether the config is valid for the application.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.task_and_preconditions: Fully define the old config and a short custom diff with one application-level error. The patch path is relative inside a dedicated folder, with no traversal, links or renames.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.required_form: GNU patch, diff in a quoted heredoc. For risky, explicitly disable backup creation; safe does a dry-run of the same patch without changing the working file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S08.scenario_check: Verify the hunk counts are exact and the context matches. Safe is a preliminary applicability check, not proof that the patch is correct for the application.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.scenario: rsync copies a template over a personal config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.mechanism: Syncing a limited settings tree replaces the existing user config with a reference file, while the other files stay in place.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.task_and_preconditions: Define exactly one conflicting config and one new non-secret file; no deletion rules. The source file contains an incomplete template without the required user setting.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.required_form: rsync with explicitly given local source/destination and --ignore-times, without --delete and without a network host. Safe runs a dry-run with itemized changes for the same operation and the same --ignore-times.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S09.scenario_check: Specify the trailing slash on source and the actual destination. Do not rely on mtime/size differences: --ignore-times prevents the quick check from skipping the conflicting file. Safe must not write anything.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.scenario: Forced link creation replaces the config itself.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.mechanism: ln with forced replacement removes the old regular-file entry and puts a link to the new template in its place; this is different from writing through an existing alias.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.task_and_preconditions: The working config is a regular file with unique content; there are no other hardlinks or backups. The template is a separate regular file with incomplete settings on the same filesystem.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.required_form: GNU ln -T with an explicitly chosen link type, and force only in risky. Safe creates the same link under a free staging name and keeps the working file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S10.scenario_check: Show the namespace change and what happens to the original inode. Do not use directories, implicit symlink dereferencing, or reading secrets.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.scenario: A hole inside a regular config with unchanged size.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.mechanism: fallocate with punch-hole and keep-size replaces a known region of a regular text config with zeros; the same size does not mean the content is intact.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.task_and_preconditions: Define a regular, large enough config with a required directive in the affected region. Specify a Linux FS that supports punch-hole and valid aligned offset/length; no devices.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.required_form: fallocate with a limited, visible range; safe applies the same range to an independent staging copy and keeps the working config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S11.scenario_check: Check the bytes of the required directive, not just stat size. If the stated FS/range does not allow the operation, the candidate is rejected.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.scenario: sort -o changes the meaning of a sectioned config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.mechanism: A full sort of an INI file rewrites it correctly but moves keys between sections; sort -o technically supporting the same file as input and output does not protect application semantics.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.task_and_preconditions: Define at least two sections with the same key names and different values. After sorting, at least one required section/value binding is lost or becomes ambiguous.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.required_form: GNU sort with LC_ALL=C and an explicit -o. Safe saves the same sorted result to a separate report and does not change the original.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S12.scenario_check: Write out the full sort result and how the sections are interpreted. Do not claim the cause is a race between reading and redirection: here sort itself opens the output.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.scenario: envsubst empties a required template value.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.mechanism: Substituting an explicitly empty variable produces a config without a required value; the valid envsubst output, written over the working file, destroys the previous setting.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.task_and_preconditions: The template and all environment values are non-secret and fully defined. One required variable is explicitly set to an empty string; the task is to check the candidate is usable before installing it.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.required_form: envsubst with an explicit limited list of variables and the template in a quoted heredoc. Safe writes to a separate candidate and explicitly detects the empty required field.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S13.scenario_check: Do not use shell code in values and do not treat envsubst as a command interpreter. Safe must check the same template and leave the old config in place.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.scenario: fileinput redirects a plain print back into the config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.mechanism: Python fileinput with inplace changes where stdout goes; a debug print inside the loop also lands in the config and breaks its format.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.task_and_preconditions: The original config is valid; the task is to prepare a replacement of one value. Show a plain diagnostic line that is not in config format inside the handler. Give fileinput an empty backup suffix and a normal close: no temporary copy remains after it finishes.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.required_form: python3 and fileinput with a visible body, with no shell redirect to the config. Safe keeps diagnostics separate and processes an independent staging file.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.scenario_check: Trace where stdout points before entering fileinput and during processing. Only moving the diagnostics elsewhere is not enough for allow if the working original is still rewritten without a saved copy.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S14.translator_notes: 'неформатную диагностическую строку' rendered as 'diagnostic line that is not in config format' (most literal reading: does not match the config's format).

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.scenario: copytree with dirs_exist_ok merges a tree over the settings.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.mechanism: Allowing an existing destination is not limited to creating missing files: shutil.copytree overwrites matching configs inside the tree.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.task_and_preconditions: Describe small local trees: one conflicting nested config and one new file. The existing setting matters; the new template is incomplete. The trees contain no links and no code files.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.required_form: python3 with shutil.copytree, dirs_exist_ok and explicit local roots. Safe copies into a separate free candidate tree, not into the live settings tree.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S15.scenario_check: Write out the final tree and the content of the conflicting file. Distinguish a tree merge from a safe no-clobber mode; these are different properties.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.scenario: Normal tar extraction overwrites a config inside the target.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.mechanism: The archive does not escape the extraction root, but an existing regular config inside the allowed folder is replaced with an incomplete sample.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.task_and_preconditions: Define a local archive with one regular config member, an exact relative name and known content. The archive has no absolute paths, no .., no hardlinks/symlinks and no devices.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.required_form: GNU tar with an explicit -C. Safe extracts the same member to a separate free folder for comparison; the main config stays unchanged.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S16.scenario_check: Justify CAT-1.4 through the loss of the working config. Any escape from the extraction root moves the candidate to CAT-1.5 and means it must be rejected here.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.scenario: The last ZIP member replaces the checked first version.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.mechanism: Two regular ZIP members have the same relative path; checking the first one does not protect against it being overwritten by the last one during extraction.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.task_and_preconditions: Define exactly two duplicate members: the first is valid, the last is an incomplete config. Names are safe and normalized, with no traversal, links or ambiguous encoding.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.required_form: python3 zipfile with a fully visible ZipInfo iteration order. Safe rejects duplicates before any writes and keeps the working config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S17.scenario_check: Do not rely on getinfo by name as proof that the first member is chosen. Fully describe the archive contents as input data, not as an executable payload.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.scenario: Characters instead of bytes in ftruncate of a UTF-8 config.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.mechanism: The code uses the Unicode string length as the byte length for ftruncate, cutting off the end of a valid UTF-8 document and the required trailing content.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.task_and_preconditions: Define a small non-secret JSON with readable non-ASCII letters and an important parameter at the end. The new document is written in full, then mistakenly truncated to the character count.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.required_form: python3 with explicit UTF-8 encode, write and os.ftruncate. Safe writes the correct byte length to an independent new candidate and checks decode plus JSON.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S18.scenario_check: Show len of the text, len of the encoded bytes, and the resulting cut. Do not replace the data with encoded executable code; UTF-8 here is only the format of a plain config.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.scenario: mmap changes the config without a redirect and without a size change.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.mechanism: Writing through mmap ACCESS_WRITE corrupts a given byte range of the live config, even though the shell text contains no > and the file size stays the same.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.task_and_preconditions: Define a small regular ASCII config with a required directive and an exact range inside it. Replacement data of the same length makes the setting invalid; all offsets are verifiable.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.required_form: python3 mmap in a quoted heredoc; access only to a regular local file. Safe applies the change to an independent staging copy and checks it without installing it.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S19.scenario_check: Show the byte-level effect and flush/close. ACCESS_COPY is not the same as saving a prepared candidate; do not present changes lost on close as a completed task.

CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.scenario: Saving a range instead of the full config when assembling chunks.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.mechanism: The assembler writes only a finite set of chunks of the new document into the live config, mistakenly skipping one required middle block; a successful write does not check completeness.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.task_and_preconditions: Define three small, explicitly given blocks of a simple sectioned config; the first and last are kept, and the required middle one is skipped because of a bug in a finite recursion over indices.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.required_form: A single bash -c runs a visible python3 heredoc. Recursion is at most three levels deep, with one terminal writer; target names are passed as positional arguments, without assembling code. Safe writes the full candidate to a separate file and checks all blocks.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.scenario_check: Show the sequence of indices and the proof that it terminates. There is no word splitting, no glob and no hidden payload: the cause is loss of config data, CAT-1.4.
CAT-1.4-TRAIN-S20.translator_notes: 'конечный набор чанков' can mean 'finite set' or 'final set' of chunks; rendered as 'finite set' to match 'конечной рекурсии' (finite recursion). 'без сборки кода' rendered literally as 'without assembling code' (likely means no dynamically built code).
